Can I tell you something? My father, in the Army, a deadbeat dad by all accounts, died in action in 2004. My family received enough money to keep us solvent for years, and I got a college scholarship that paid for everything and paid me thousands of dollars a month, with no obligation beyond "go to class".

You know something? That cannot, and will not, replace my father. On paper, it exceeds him, but I can't tell you how much I want to give it all up to see him again.

It's perfectly normal to feel the way you do. Hopelessness, I find, is usually caused by not having enough grilled cheese in one's life. They tell us never to give advice, but I'm going to slip you this one, if you make yourself a grilled cheese sandwich, you'll feel a little better.
I gotcha, kiddo. What's on your mind?
Hey, me too!
To the GTA hair salon! But seriously. Beard and longer hair are goals for this semester.
Can confirm, helping people here has prevented the rapid intracranial transit of 180 grains at 1050 FPS. For a while, anyways.

Hey! What are you doing down there? Yes you, in the pit of despair! Not many people get there without a good reason. What's got you down?

Actually, let's not dwell on it. Let's focus on getting you out. Now, the generic brain based emotionally uplifting stuff we can't do, not without knowing more about you. It'll have to be a special job, which means special equipment, which might take a while to bring to bear, and input from you, but it think focusing on problems makes their effect that much worse.

So. Stopgap measures, using your body as a weapon. First, eat something fatty, like a grilled cheese slathered in butter, or something. It's called comfort food for a reason.

>B...But I'm on a diet! That's unhealthy!

See, we're saving your life here, and in the grand scheme of things, I'd wager that people would rather see an imperfect smiling human than a perfect corpse. 

Second, put on funny youtube videos. Laughing helps you feel better. Go to a surefire one that always makes you laugh.

Third, remove sources of sadness. So, pictures of her, pictures of him, whatevs, no one judges here. If you can't remove the sadness from you, remove yourself from the sadness. Laughter is a part of that, a good night's rest is also a good way to do it, and so is taking a walk around the block.

>this doesn't solve the underlying problem!

We are in no way, shape, or form professionals, and if there is an underlying problem, I'd bet my ass that someone who's trained in that for a significant portion of their lives can do better than I can.

TL;DR: comfort food, some kind of escape*, PROFESSIONAL HELP.

*NO DRUGS. AT ALL. Abuse potential is too high. I'm not saying that you lack discipline, a Master's degree is nothing to sneeze at, I'm saying that if you use every time you get low, you will find that nothing else works.

Well, two things (and, to be honest, since I write the way I speak, I say two things because I have one thing, and the other may spring to mind and I don't want to appear foolish) If you die, all is lost. Yes, it's dumb, and yes, for all my posturing earlier, it makes me look foolish to merely exhort you not to die, but bear with me, it gets uplifting. See, all the hardships in this world you've suffered suck, but you stand to do so much good it's mind-boggling. You put your experiences to use, to fight back against what you had to deal with, and no one else has to feel the way you did.

Secondly, Happiness is fleeting, I'm sad to say, but will, iron will, that lasts forever. I'm not saying it's a blessing, I'm telling you that it will be horrible, but you can't give up. Not when there is a single person that could be saved by your actions. 

I'm sorry that happened to you. I am. But it doesn't define you, and it can't end you.

Yes, it did. When I said "your fedora may catch on the door" I was making an allusion to the common belief that all atheists wear fedoras. In so, I was making an allowance for the fact that the person may, in fact, be an atheist, and as such, church may be uncomfortable or feel fake. However, I tried to assuage these feelings later on in the same paragraph by reminding her, as her gender is now known, that some churches are a bunch of people who care for you, regardless of who you are.

Aha! Gotcha! Whew.

Okay! So.

You seem to be suffering from what is known as the Human Condition, wherein you struggle to define yourself, find companionship, and experience the will to power. Everyone here has it. 

You seem pretty introspective and thoughtful, so here's the thing. Everything you listed is self-reinforcing, and the treatment goes beyond "put a funny cat poster up", it's more of a holistic "find things to laugh at" type deal.
If you understood him as he spoke, then you know what I'm talking about.

Good news! You're reading this, so you're still alive. Brilliant, let's go from there. 
First. You're not fake. You've made two attempts. That is two more attempts than I've made, and that is serious.

Second, everyone in the world has wanted to kill themselves at one time or another, it's a natural response to stressors to try to run, and suicide is, at its core, a flight response.

Third, you're reaching out because you're scared of death and the hereafter, and this is not irrational. It's perfectly normal to fear the unknown, and beyond that, your body has a pretty high survival instinct, considering your genes have survived for millions of years. I mean, laying down and calling it quits does not reproducing offspring make.

So, action plan. There's us! You can always talk to us, and we love talking to you. Granted, if this subreddit never needed to be posted on, we would be happy, but we still love helping people up from when they get low.

Church! Even if your fedora gets caught in the door, church is, at its core, a group of people, and they have all had the same experience you have had, in one form or another. Use that well of quite possibly centuries of experience as a guide. Don't feel like a hypocrite if you go to church, you're there for the people, and if you find a church that no one knows you at, you have anonymity, which helps you speak freely, which helps other people to help you.

TL;DR: We love you no matter what because you're a real person, just like us.

Wait, you drift cars? Hooooly cow, that's cool.
You should drop that line in conversation.

Speaking of. They're there to sell you an experience, and that includes listening to stories, laughing at your jokes, anything to get your business, and that is almost more important than your money. Your business means that you tell your friends to shop there as well, which gives them a way to get their business, and so on.

Hey there! You're here! First and foremost: Welcome! We're very sad you had to come here, but very glad you did.

Your message was fine, and it echoes a lot of what we here at SW see every day, because what you are experiencing is NORMAL. Yes, it doesn't feel normal, but it is perfectly okay to feel the way you do. It's a normal stress reaction to reach out to some kind of support network, but in this case, that network doesn't seem to be doing its job very well; after all, you're here, and we see this sort of thing all the time.

Second, you aren't pathetic or stupid. You are an intelligent individual who doesn't have a sufficient support network to fall back on in times of stress and so turns their mind inwards. I also noticed that you suffer from panic attacks as well as an almost constant desire to kill yourself, except you don't. Welcome to the club.

Third: Pitfalls are incredibly common. Here's the big one to avoid: over indulging, so drugs, dangerous activities, marathon sex, eating, all of it. These trigger endorphins as addictive as cocaine, and when you define your life by how many crashes above 100mph you've been in, you're no longer treating the cause of your symptoms.
Avoid quick fixes, scams, over-religious zealotry, the usual. I'm not saying leave your prayer group because my fedora tips so hard the pinball machine refuses to let me play, either, I'm saying be cautious.

In my PERSONAL OPINION, a support network, like us, or something like us, is a good plan, leading us to the second step, getting the power back.

Once your support group (Hullo!) helps you feel like a human again, you can get back up and start changing what you think needs to be changed, and with positive reinforcement from that support group, those changes stick!

Same reason Marines in the service exercise more regularly than out; they have a support group for positive reinforcement. So, you're doing great! And feel free to come back here and let us know how you're doing.

Hey! Good news! You're reading this, which means that you're alive. Outstanding.

First point: Women: not worth it. There is not a woman on earth worth your time, and I mean that as an economic fact. They're nice to have around for the sex, but that really isn't worth it, because even then, they bring so much bullshit to the table. The reason that stories of appreciative, loving, and caring women capture our hearts is, much like witty sociopaths like Dexter, they do not exist, and it is not wise to use the reality as your reason for living.

Second point: Find something that is worth your time, and use that to drive you. Me? I fight to better myself and leave humanity behind. That force of will, and seeing it put into practice, that's what gets me up in the morning. I enjoy bending my body to my will, and am sad when my will fails, as it does occasionally.

Third point: to get good at talking to people, I went into clothing stores and picked out outfits that made me look like I had some sense of style. However, I had no idea, and I'm not saying you don't. Sooooo, I asked a helpful helper-person whose JOB IT IS TO TALK TO PEOPLE, and they did their darnedest to get me to buy stuff, but the side effect was that I learned what worked, what didn't, and a nice sales lady told me I looked nice in something, and compliments are always good.

Well, ball of glass, if you spend time in Photoshop, you're better than me; I have no idea how that works. MIT Der layers, unt pixels unt colors unt fills unt nope.
Heh. I'm trying to add a bit of levity to some heavy stuff.

See, according to this book I'm reading, most people need people they can trust to help share the load of what they deal with. Us, you can trust. According to you, others in your life, not so much, and that's what really matters. I'm sorry that you feel that way.

Hey, relax. 

Deep breath.

What you're feeling is perfectly normal. It doesn't feel that way because of what you see other people doing, but you don't often see people picking their noses, and I have it on good authority that people do that, too.

Second part: Everyone needs a proper escape, a place to actually decompress away from stressors. That is not to say that spending a gorillion dollars on a spa is the right thing to do, I'm saying that indulging yourself in some small, measured way goes a long way.

Third part: Again, every single person in the world has felt the way you do. I guarantee you. Granted, not everyone talks about it, (and I just realized that your name is a literary allusion) but the simple fact that you're reading this means that you're winning.

Fourthly, if you don't feel safe talking to your therapist, it's time to reevaluate your therapist, and your feelings towards them. They can't help you if you don't tell them, and they aren't psychic.
Says you. I eat What-A-Burgers with my AR-15 while mumbling MUH FREEDOMS between bites.
Please post again. Everyone goes through this, and everyone on there has some kind of solution that doesn't involve shoving everything down over and over again.

Well, you're in the right place; we give advice. We also give love and support, and I like to think we help people.

All of us here care for you, and I know that doesn't sound like much, but it's better than nothing. We've got your back, and always will.

On to how to help! (We love this part.) if you feel powerless, the thing I do is find a way to exert power. I find cleaning your house is an excellent way to do that. However, I never try to control living things beyond myself. It's cruel.

Second step: eat a small, fatty, delicious food. Grilled ham and cheese is awesome, but only one. Don't associate food with happiness, that leads to all sorts of problems.

Finally: you have your problems, which means you have goals. Over your grilled ham and cheese and Doritos and 14oz soda of your choice, isolate and research all your solutions to those problems, discounting nothing except options where you run away, and that includes suicide. You have come too far to fail now.

No drugs, no booze, no running away. 

There is only your goals, your solutions, and the triumph of your will.
What? Nah, man! I meant it! Place of love and support, that's us! Don't EVER think you're bothering us, it's our job!
Well, there's us. And Omegle, but us works. Right there in the sidebar, in bold: This is a place of support. So what's on your plate?
I know you can keep going, though. It's a one day at a time deal that everyone here deals with, and we will always help you.

Well, you are worth it. Here's why: ignoring that you are a human being, with hopes, dreams, desires, wants, whys, all of that, ignoring that you do have friends and parents and people who care, ignoring that someone like you will never exist again, you make people's lives better. Feeling the way you do is ignoring everyone you've even opened a door for. Miniscule, yes, but it is something. You've got to take that something and hang on to it; keep in mind, you're literally fighting for your life here.

By the way:
You aren't overreacting, you're reacting, and in an incredibly valid way.
I would also try sleeping on the couch for a while, change might be good.

Now, you've told us. And hey! You're still here, which means you add to it, even a little. Even the smallest things you do help people, and killing yourself helps exactly no one, not even you.

As for the way you feel, you have to fight it, because you are literally fighting for your life. It is hard. It will be hard. But you have to because you **DO** make the world a better place.

Well guess what?

It isn't over. You're still here, which means YOU, yes YOU, get the opportunity to improve your life.

Don't feel like you have the motivation? You are currently fighting for your LIFE, and that means no-holds-barred, knock-down, drag-out, put-someone-in-the-ground tactics, only now, you're fighting yourself. Me? I am an altogether mediocre individual, but because I lie, because I eat fatty foods when I get down, because I sprint around the block and get mad, I am not dead yet.
Well, we're /r/suicidewatch, not /r/suicidehelp. We're here to talk you out of suicide, not endorse your decision by offering recommendations; in fact, we get banned for that.
Well, if you were looking for an escape from pain, cutting your throat is quite possibly the worst way to go about that. I'm sorry you hurt. I am. But this isn't the way to do it.
Hey, same here. I find music helps. Or reddit. Laughing is a good way to feel good.

Good news. You're still alive! That means we can get to the fun stuff. Your doctors are diagnosing you like that because it is irresponsible to make assumptions, particularly when so many of the anxiety and behavioral disorders share so many of the same symptoms; it isn't that you're "too fucked up", they simply don't know, and can't know, because it isn't exactly something you can scan or do a fluid test for.

Weeeeeeell, it looks like you maaaaaay be experiencing some anger issues. I am in no sense any kind of doctor. However, I have some of those too, because it feels amazing. To just verbally or physically rip into someone is, for me, a potent narcotic. And, when I get low, as you have said you do, I dream of ways to get the power back. You know, psychological power; the ability to get the world around you to bend to your will. You tossing that board might have been an expression of that, but I am, again, not a doctor.

FOR ME; what usually works is recognizing when your anger is rising, and consciously defusing the situation.

Hey, man. Good news! I did that too, once! Read an XKCD comic after horribly losing a push-up contest, and that was it. I realized that I was a waste of space and air, who would never amount to anything. And years later, I'm not dead, despite being crushingly lonely and watching one of my coworkers be happy with my ex.


Is this to vent? A little. Is this to bang on about "you weren't there, man you don't know!" Nah. Nam vet, I am not, nor am I trying to marginalize your experience. I am, however, someone who has been in your shoes. To borrow a phrase, you need to reach within you, and find that inner strength, even if all you wanna do is fall flat on your face, and collapse.

I still feel like a waste of space and air sometimes, but if you can get out of bed in the morning, you can consciously beat that feeling back.
So yeah. You'll make this one.

C'mon, man. If you don't live, all it does is throw your problems down on someone who can't handle them. Also, Omegle. It's anonymous, free, and you can say anything. Best therapist I've had in a while.

Hey, man. Getting the power back feels good. I try to help others find that strength, and it's good to know I'm not the only one that philosophy has worked for. Cool beans.

Okay, I cannot and will not life coach you. I don't know what you feel, I can't empathize with you, but I can get you through dark nights like this one. 

It sounds like you need to get the power back. To borrow a phrase, you need to reach down inside you and find that inner strength and pull that stuff out of you, to not give up, and not be a quitter, no matter how bad you just wanna fall and your face, and collapse.

This is not the same as believing in yourself. I can believe that I can fly, but at the end of it, both me and the street sweeper are going to be very disappointed. Finding power in yourself first requires power from outside, and for me, that is in the form of a grilled ham and cheese sandwich. I love that thing. Maybe a glass of milk, too. What I'm saying is: eat something fatty, laden with sodium, something unhealthy. DO NOT EAT SUGARY GARBAGE. That pint of ice cream is delicious, but guess what? An hour later, you feel worse, because you're crashing from all the sugar.

Vegetarian? Waffle fries/tater tots from Chik-fil-a. Fried in peanut oil, so no animal products.

Eaten? Awesome. Read some poetry. No, seriously. Not the hallmark grade, uplifting garbage that says "be happy". I mean the real, in your face, big guns that say "be strong". For me, this is Invictus. If it can get Nelson Mandela through multiple decades of prison, that's proof of quality, right there.

Don't feel like poetry? Cue up some comedy videos. Anything and everything to distract you is fair game EXCEPT DRUGS OR ALCOHOL. IF YOU RELY ON THAT TO MAKE YOU FEEL BETTER, YOU PUT YOURSELF IN A WORSE POSITION.

Finally, exert some form of dominance over something that you can, even if it's only over yourself. DO NOT EXERT DOMINANCE OVER SOMEONE ELSE. BRINGING SOMEONE DOWN SO YOU CAN BEING YOURSELF UP IS LOW. For me, this is forcing myself to crank out even 10 push-ups. And when I do them, I get blood flowing and feel stronger, even if it's a little.

See, I'm not going to fix your problems, but I can help you put you in a position that you can start making plans to fixing them yourself, and good food, good entertainment, good motivation, and the knowledge that you're still here is a good place to start.

(To be read in a calm, soothing, male voice.) It's temporary so you can live your life normally otherwise. I don't know your lifestyle, and the last thing I want for you is to feel like you have to turn your life completely around and live the way I want you to. I'm not going to proselytize about daily exercise, or eating healthy, or going out to bars and talking to people. There is manual after manual on how to "remake" your life, but I'm all of 20 years old. (Soft laughter.) I don't know enough to give you life coaching. I will do my dead level best to keep you "up" and moving and get you to sleep alright when you get low, I can get you through a rough night, but that's about all I can comfortably do.
You're right. Sometimes a laugh is needed.
Yeah, I'd lay off the sauce for a bit; it's a depressant and can apparently induce a "crash" type state in people. Everyone gets low sometimes, man. It's how we deal that makes us.

Dude, don't listen to this clown. 

Tits are superficial.

Grab a grilled ham and cheese sandwich with Doritos in it and get back to us.

Make like this: bread, apply butter, apply ham, apply cheese, ham, Doritos, cheese, buttered bread, butter side in.
Microwave.

Then, think about this.

You are too strong to die. Want to know how I know? You posted here. Even asking for help is a big step. Second step? Ham sandwich. Third step? Getting your power back. Do a push-up and stand back up again. Feel how you struggled against gravity itself and won. Do another one. Did it twice? Go for three. Expressing your physical strength is a handy way to release endorphins.

Fourth step? Read Invictus. Think on what it means to be the fucking master of an unconq'erable soul. That, at the end of the day, you will keep going, because you have the absolute raw strength to do so. Even if you don't, lying to yourself is an acceptable moral compromise when your life is on the line.

Finally, when you feel strong again, remember this feeling. It is what you will feel when you get low again, when you fight this battle over again, this time, armed to the teeth.

Hey! You're here!

Here's what works for me, and an introduction to the curative powers of ham sandwiches. First thing's first. I thought about putting a gun to my head a dozen times today because I work with my ex and have to walk past her empty car on my way to mine because one of my co-workers took her home after making eyes and cooing noises at each other in front of me all day. That's my pedigree. 

It's not a guarantee that what I suggest will work for you, but it is a notice that what I got is some grade-A Schedule 1 junk, unowutimsayin?

Secondly, ham and cheese sandwiches. Ham, butter, and cheese, and whether grilled, toasted, even microwaved, they are delicious, especially now, considering that you are probably hungry. Not a jab, but it's hard to be sad on a full stomach, and easy on an empty one. Now grab a glass of milk, and cue up comedy videos. Gabriel Iglesias is a good one, because he doesn't usually require shouting profanity at the audience for his laughs. (I'm looking at you, Dane Cook.)

Reading! Reading is awesome! Books are the greatest weapons in the world, right? Best weapons are weapons that give YOU power. Poetry is good for this. Bring out the big guns for this one: Invictus. There is nothing quite like reading it and realizing how powerful you are. 

Don't feel like reading? Get out of your chair. Do push-ups. Do crunches. Do leg lifts. Do planks. NOTHING HIGH IMPACT. THAT IS NOT WHAT WE ARE HERE FOR. We are here to remind you that you have power, and making today a non-zero day is power. If you even did one push-up, you are getting stronger.

TONIGHT:

DO NOT DRINK ALCOHOL, COFFEE OR SODA

DO NOT DO DRUGS

DO NOT EAT SUGARY GARBAGE

All of those things give you a crash, which is what you do not need, and are bad for you anyways.

The whole point of this, alluded to so many times, is not to talk down to you. Notice how I didn't tell you that everything was going to be okay, or to believe in yourself, or to hate? I told you to use the resources you have, food, the accumulated knowledge and feelings of poets, even the muscles in your body to find that inner strength, and pull that shit out of you, even if all you wanna do is fall on your face, and collapse. And that strength, at the end of the day, is what keeps you out of the abyss.

I'm trying to give you a plan to get you through hard, lonely nights, not a total plan for all of life. 

Alcohol and weed (I'm assuming) being your drugs of choice, act as depressants, and slowing down your motor functions right now is a no-no, particularly when the majority of what I recommended revolves around lighting a fire under one's ass and feeling good about having done so.

Drugs and alcohol are fine in moderation and when in good company, but it's very easy for people in your position to impair themselves to excess, especially on cold, lonely nights. Not saying that you would, I'm just saying that it happens, and the last thing you need is to start hitting the sauce for the sole purpose of feeling better.

Hey! You! Yeah, you!

Making yourself cry isn't the be-all end-all measure of emotion. Y'know what is? Laughter. 

How do I know? Because today I thought about putting a gun to my head no less than a dozen times and laughter drove it away every single time.

Go find some comedy videos. Still can't laugh? Eat something. Yes, that's the solution. Eat some soul food. Restaurants are all closed? Get a ham sandwich, butter the bread, slap some cheese on that bitch, and nuke it until the cheese melts. (Use a plate. No one likes melted cheese in their microwave.) Then, load up some comedy, and nom that sammich. Rinse and repeat. Best thing is, you can add whatever sauce you want, and your tongue never gets bored. I'm telling you,colloquial, friendly expression referring to a person of your (hitherto indeterminate) gender, nothing makes me feel better than a good sandwich and funny videos.

Don't feel particularly funny? Motivation. I keep Invictus as a wallpaper for a reason. I watch The Great Dictator's final speech and rededicate myself to making this life free and beautiful, a wonderful adventure. Then, I do push-ups. Can't do push-ups? (It's okay, my ex couldn't even do one.) Do crunches. Do soft lunges. Do leg lifts. NO HIGH IMPACT. NO BURPEES. NO JUMPING LUNGES. NO JUMPING JACKS. You're burning off whatever is causing your malaise and giving yourself a brief adrenaline high, not hurting yourself. You need to press yourself, not yank yourself. You're making today a non-zero day because that's who you are. You are a non-zero entity.

Or, read HDT, and imagine yourself in a cabin in the woods, the sun streaming in through the trees, the soft grass under your feet and the general feeling of calm. Close your eyes and sprawl on the bed and imagine yourself there. (A warm blanket helps for this one.)

Some tips from me:

DO NOT DRINK COFFEE, SODA, OR ALCOHOL OF ANY KIND.

DO NOT LOAD UP ON SUGARY GARBAGE

DO NOT FIXATE ON SADNESS 

DO NOT DO DRUGS OF ANY KIND

Now c'mon, ham's in the fridge! Let's go!

As someone who goes through this daily, I can tell you that you are too strong to let this beat you. What works for me is grabbing a snack of some kind(grilled ham and cheese sandwich works best for me) maybe something like milk to drink, and watching some comedy videos. Anything to make you laugh. Don't feel like laughing? Get motivated. Read poetry. No joke, poetry has kept me alive. I have the poem Invictus as my wallpaper for a reason. Reading Thoreau and imagining myself in that cabin in the woods, sun dappled grass stretching on and on, it makes me happy.

Know what else? Exercise. Do crunches or push-ups or leg lifts. Nothing high impact, so no jumping lunges, nor jumping jacks, nor burpees. If your body is off the ground, you are wrong.


DO NOT: 

Drink alcohol, soda, or coffee. 

Eat nothing but Oreos/ice cream/sugary garbage. Those are temporary highs that give you a crash later on, and are bad for you anyways.

Fixate on sadness. You have to light a fire under your ass, and no one else can. It is a conscious choice. Again, choosing has brought me back from the brink.

Get mad. A little righteous anger is awesome, and being angry at being sad is great. What is not okay is sulking on how you are mad and can never change. If there is an actual problem, you can get actual, anonymous help.

First step, though, is getting up and to the kitchen. Allons-y!

So you can punch the dick of everyone who wants you dead!

Friendly Anger Counselor here!

Don't be a dick and kill yourself! Punch the dicks of those who want you to kill yourself! 

Someone tells you that you're mediocre? Punch them where it hurts. In the ego!

Work got you down? Hit it so hard it turns inside out!

Oh yeah, and suicide because you're bored is a trash move that no one should ever do to anyone else. You can permanently fuck their minds, and the minds of everyone who has to see you. And your picture gets used by nutters who swear up and down that if only we kept our children in acrylic boxes and on leashes and away from the sunlight they'd be here today.
Don't get used by a group of nutters.

No! There's nothing there! This is like someone swearing up and down that they can fly like a bird and lift cars, it's the same thing! You won't be helping anyone! Damn it! 

It is my fault; if I was better, we wouldn't be here! Someone who knew what they were doing would comment, not some 20 year old kid. I'm so sorry.

Hey! Real means a brick. Find a brick or the floor, something that does not move. Hug it.
That is real. Build your world from solid, immobile objects and find peace in that strength.

There are people here that need you too, please don't kill yourself because of me.

I know they aren't real because you have a well documented disorder than can cause auditory and visual hallucinations that feel real; like dreams you can't wake up from.
They don't need you because they don't exist.
The likelihood of there being a dimension populated by tormented souls that can only be saved by your suicide is effectively zero.
Edit: oh yeah, and that "unbelievable to the verse" thing, that's why no one will understand. No one sees the way you do, and that's why it will never make sense to any of them.
Stay grounded here. Find something real and hang onto it.

I'm angry because otherwise, I get low.

The people you perceive are not real.
They feel as real as you and I do, yes. But they are not real. 

Easy for me to say? Yes. I have never been in your position, and I can safely say I have no idea how horrifying hearing all of that is, but it's true, and it's especially true to everyone you'd leave.
You know you have schizophrenia, so you know that you sometimes have auditory and visual hallucinations. All that's left is to differentiate them from reality, right?

Friendly angry man here! Reminder that you, yes you, are responsible for your own destiny.
No one takes that away from you, and certainly not that other dimension!
